user.text:
I want a small Next.js app for keeping track of the books I'm reading.

When I open it I want to see what I'm currently reading and what I've finished. I want to add a book from a form, mark one as finished, and click through to a book to see its title, author and my notes. I'd like to be able to send someone a link to a single book.

Nothing fancy and no accounts. Skip the database, save the books to a JSON file so they're still there after a restart.

history.assistant:
I've built the book tracker as a Next.js app (Next 16.3, React 19.3, in /workspace), and it works. To run it:

  npm run dev                       (development, http://localhost:3000)
  npm run build && npm start        (production)

What it does:
- The home page shows "Currently reading" (newest first) and "Finished" (most recently finished first, with the date). Each book in the reading list has a "Mark finished" button, and the add form (title, author, notes) is below the lists. Only the title is required.
- Clicking a book opens /books/<id>, which shows the title, author, your notes and whether it's finished. On that page you can mark it finished, edit the notes, or use "Copy link" to share it. An unknown id shows a "Book not found" page.
- Books are saved to data/books.json, which is created on first use. Two quick saves at the same time can't overwrite each other, and a crash mid-save won't leave a broken file. I added data/ to .gitignore so your reading list isn't committed; remove that line if you want it in git.

Checks I ran:
- npm test (vitest): 6 tests passed. They cover adding, requiring a title, marking finished, editing notes, 20 books added at once with none lost, and the data reaching the JSON file.
- npm run build: succeeds with no warnings.
- Against the running server, using the real forms: I added "The Hobbit", confirmed its page showed the author and notes, marked it finished, and saw it move to the Finished list. Text you type is escaped safely on the page. An unknown book id returns 404. After restarting the server, the book was still there.
- I didn't click through it in a real browser; the "Copy link" button in particular is untested.

Two things to know about sharing and having no accounts:
- The link only works if the other person can reach wherever the app is running. localhost won't work for them, so you'd need to host it somewhere. If you do, bear in mind that hosts with a read-only or temporary filesystem (like most serverless platforms) won't keep the JSON file. A small VPS or any always-on Node server will.
- Anyone who can reach the app can view every book, and can also add books, mark them finished and edit notes.

The main files are lib/books.js (the JSON store), app/page.jsx (home page), app/AddBookForm.jsx, app/actions.js (the form handlers) and app/books/[id]/page.jsx (book page). I also updated package.json with the dev/build/start/test scripts and the new dependencies. Nothing is committed.
